title: Hazel and the Contact
premise: Marguerite Pemberton, a veteran air-crash investigator, is haunted by the death of her family in row twelve of Flight 4471—an accident officially blamed on pilot error. When a stranger named Elias Voss repays a favor she has no memory of doing, he leaves behind evidence that the crash was engineered to silence a whistleblower aboard. As Marguerite digs into falsified maintenance records spanning three governments, an assassin codenamed Lark closes in on everyone who touches the file. Marguerite must smuggle the truth to an international tribunal before Lark erases the last living witness—herself—and in the end she trades her own anonymity for justice, testifying publicly and finally sleeping through the night.
about_author: Casper Ravensworth is the pen name of a former aviation-industry analyst who spent a decade writing safety reports no one read. They now write thrillers about the people who read them anyway.

chapters.title: Row Twelve
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Three years after the crash that killed her husband and daughter, she still investigates other people's disasters by day and replays row twelve by night. A routine inspection reveals an anomaly in Flight 4471's tail assembly records. Emotional beat: grief sharpening into suspicion.

chapters.title: The Favor That Never Happened
chapters.summary: A stranger, Elias Voss, appears at her office door claiming she once saved his life—a debt she cannot remember. He leaves a sealed envelope: maintenance logs proving 4471 was sabotaged. POV alternates briefly to Voss watching her from across the street. Emotional beat: uncanny vertigo, the ground shifting under memory.

chapters.title: Interest Owed
chapters.summary: Marguerite verifies the logs against her own archived data; they're authentic—and they implicate a contractor with government ties. That night her apartment is searched, professionally, leaving nothing disturbed but her sense of safety. Emotional beat: fear arriving as precision rather than chaos.

chapters.title: Lark
chapters.summary: Assassin POV. Lark receives a contract: retrieve the file, leave no witnesses. We see the methodical elegance of the work and the first name on the list—Voss. Emotional beat: cold competence that makes the reader complicit in dread.

chapters.title: Invisible No Longer
chapters.summary: Marguerite realizes her decades of deliberate low profile—no social media, unlisted everything—have been undone by one envelope. She contacts Voss through a dead-drop protocol he taught her years ago, or so he claims. Emotional beat: the hunter realizing she is prey.

chapters.title: What Elias Knew
chapters.summary: Voss explains: Marguerite testified anonymously in an old whistleblower case, saving him, then had the memory sealed by trauma therapy. The sabotage of 4471 was retaliation gone wrong—the target was the whistleblower in seat 12C, not her family. Emotional beat: guilt and rage braided together.

chapters.title: Three Governments
chapters.summary: Marguerite maps the conspiracy: a defense contractor laundering faulty parts through procurement channels in three countries, each regulator paid to look away. Her own agency is compromised. Emotional beat: institutional betrayal as personal violation.

chapters.title: The Man in Seat 12C
chapters.summary: She tracks the whistleblower's widow, Dana Okafor, who received an anonymous payout and a warning never to ask questions. Dana has kept her husband's hidden drive. POV shifts to Dana. Emotional beat: two grieving women recognizing each other across a shared crime scene.

chapters.title: Safehouse Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Voss moves them to a safehouse, but Marguerite counts exits, cameras, lies—and concludes Voss knows more than he says about who ordered the hit. First physical confrontation with one of Lark's scouts. Emotional beat: trust becoming a calculated risk.

chapters.title: Flight Recorder
chapters.summary: Dana's drive contains cockpit audio suggesting the crew fought a control failure consistent with tampering. Marguerite reconstructs the final ninety seconds of her family's flight, frame by frame. Emotional beat: the most painful chapter—grief converted into testimony.

chapters.title: A Debt Collected
chapters.summary: Lark finds Voss. Their confrontation reveals history: Lark trained Voss, or vice versa. Voss escapes wounded, passing the original favor's proof—a recording implicating the contractor's director—to Marguerite. Emotional beat: loyalty tested at gunpoint.

chapters.title: Burn Notice
chapters.summary: Marguerite's credentials are revoked; she's framed for leaking classified data. Hunted by her own agency, she goes dark using skills from her investigator past. Emotional beat: the system she served now erasing her.

chapters.title: The Quiet Courier
chapters.summary: She smuggles copies of the evidence through a network of crash-victim families—people with nothing left to lose. Each handoff raises stakes as Lark eliminates couriers. Emotional beat: solidarity forged in loss.

chapters.title: Interrogation of One
chapters.summary: Marguerite is captured briefly by agency internal affairs; she turns the interrogation around, planting doubt in a young agent, Reyes, who becomes a reluctant ally. Emotional beat: persuasion as survival weapon.

chapters.title: Lark's Ledger
chapters.summary: Lark POV. A rare interior chapter: the assassin begins questioning the contract's origin, discovering the client wants not just silence but the destruction of exculpatory evidence. Emotional beat: the instrument developing a conscience.

chapters.title: The Tribunal Window
chapters.summary: Reyes confirms an international aviation tribunal convenes in ten days—the only forum outside all three governments' reach. Getting the evidence admitted requires a living witness willing to testify on record. Emotional beat: hope with a deadline.

chapters.title: Crossings
chapters.summary: A tense border sequence: Marguerite and Dana move the drive through checkpoints while Lark closes from two directions. Voss sacrifices himself as decoy. Emotional beat: sacrifice paying forward the favor that started it all.

chapters.title: What Stays Buried
chapters.summary: Cornered in a decommissioned hangar, Marguerite confronts Lark—not with violence but with the flight recorder audio, forcing the assassin to hear what the contract erased. Lark hesitates, then lets her go, turning on the client instead. Emotional beat: mercy as the climax's true weapon.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Climax. Marguerite testifies before the tribunal, naming names, presenting the logs, the audio, and Lark's delivered confession of the client's identity. The hearing room holds her family's photograph. Emotional beat: grief spoken aloud becomes power.

chapters.title: Reckonings
chapters.summary: Arrests cascade across three countries; the contractor's director is indicted. Reyes leaks the internal cover-up. Lark vanishes, leaving Marguerite a single line: 'Debt cleared.' Emotional beat: justice arriving incomplete but real.

chapters.title: The Long Sleep
chapters.summary: Months later, Marguerite visits the crash memorial, reads row twelve's names aloud, and—for the first time in three years—sleeps through the night. She takes a new post training honest investigators. Emotional beat: rest earned, belonging rebuilt.

chapters.title: Epilogue: Interest Compounded
chapters.summary: Final short chapter, mixed POV. Somewhere, another whistleblower opens an envelope from a stranger who owes them nothing—and everything. Marguerite, revealed as the sender, walks away unseen. Emotional beat: the cycle of quiet justice continues.
